title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Conclusion
text: “So? Gaelion. What do you want?”
“Cure!”
He takes the box he’s been carrying on his back and holds it out to me. Given how this is going, I guess it’s chocolate after all.
“Oh, so you’ve got a chocolate gift too?”
“Cure!”
“Where’s your dad, Gaelion? He’s been quiet lately.”
“It’s not like he’s been silent. I’ve just been letting this guy do as he pleases.”
Huh… I was sure he’d vanished because his consciousness fusion had progressed too far. If I told him what I just thought, he’d probably get mad.
“Cure, Cure!”
Gaelion opened the box and handed me the chocolate inside. It seems to be giving off a strange sheen… Just to be safe, I’ll check it.
Legendary Chocolate | Quality: National Treasure Class

Whoa! The appraisal screen is blazing with light—it’s way too bright. What the heck is “Legendary Chocolate”?! And the quality isn’t just “Top Quality”—it says “National Treasure Class”! So there’s actually something even higher than that?
“Wow… it smells so good!”

Hearing that, I take a whiff of the chocolate. What is this? It smells absolutely amazing. It’s supposed to be the scent of chocolate, but it feels like a much more refined, noble fragrance. It naturally stimulates my appetite, almost as if it’s telling me I’m hungry.
“Where’d you even get chocolate like this? I want to try making it too, Filo.”
“Cureeeeeee!”
Gaelion growls menacingly at Filo, who’s drooling and creeping closer, as if to say, “I’m not giving this to you.”
“Cure! Cure, cure!”
“Huh… So you heard about the legendary chocolate, gathered ingredients from all over the world, and made it yourself? Did you finally get the recipe from a chocolate monster?”
“Is that right?”

Come to think of it, I feel like Gaelion has been making chocolate nonstop lately. Since he’s good at temperature control, he’s been helping everyone make chocolate in the kitchen. Then, just when I thought he was gone, he’d come back before I knew it and was enthusiastically working on his own chocolate. Was all that practice and studying just to make this chocolate? What on earth struck a chord with Gaelion that made him create something with such passion?
“So? What did you do with that amazing chocolate?”
“Cure! Cure!”
“He said he wants you to eat it, Master.”
“Ah, so that’s Gaelion’s take on Valentine’s Day.”
I’m not so tactless as to brush off a gesture of genuine affection. I take a bite of the chocolate Gaelion handed me.
Huh? This is amazing.

A sweetness that melts in my mouth spreads out, accompanied by a faint hint of bitterness. Yet it’s not cloying; just as I think the flavor has faded away cleanly, the bitterness intensifies, and a subtle herbal aroma fills my mouth, resetting the taste. And yet, the chocolate’s unique flavor washes over my tongue in wave after wave—like a wild dragon swarm attacking me—with the desperate, regal dignity of a king… creating an illusion. In the midst of such a desperate situation, the chocolate dashes in, defeats the dragons, saves me, and carries me away on a horse. Yes… this is the Chocolate Hero!
Wait, what is this delusion?! And it’s kind of annoying, too. Don’t strike a pose with a “glint” in your eyes, Chocolate! Anyway, it was an incredible piece of chocolate.
“This is pretty damn good.”
“Cure! Cure!”

As I eat the chocolate, Gaelion is jumping for joy. Did you make such amazing chocolate just for me? I’ll give you credit for that selfless attitude. Just as I thought he was spinning around to express his joy, Gaelion starts chirping “Cure, Cure.”
“Hmm… Stop it, just stop! Don’t you dare say any more of that!”
Interrupted by the parent Gaelion, the baby Gaelion looked distressed. But the baby Gaelion still chirped “Cure, Cure” at me.
“Um…”
Filo was listening too and looked annoyed. What’s going on? I’m super curious.
“What did you say?”
“Filo doesn’t want to say.”

Just then, Filo’s stray strand of hair stands on end, and her mouth starts speaking on its own. That’s right, as if speaking on Gaelion’s behalf. Filo tries to stop it with her hand, but perhaps caught off guard, she can’t quite resist.
‘Huh!? You Queen of Filolial! You’re trying to have these words translated so you can kick me out, aren’t you!’
It feels like some kind of otherworldly battle has begun. Fitoria must be trying to make Filo say the very words she doesn’t want to say.
“You stay silent too! Don’t say another word—Guh!?”
“Cure, cure, cure!”
“Gaelion loves his master so much he wants to make him his lifelong partner—so he doesn’t even care about the monsters in the village!”
“Huh… Come to think of it, I’ve never heard Gaelion say anything like that… ‘Life partner’?”
Is this a translation error? Isn’t Gaelion the Dragon Emperor—the greatest king of all dragons? That must be why the monster seal has already lost its effect.

And I’ve heard dragons are promiscuous creatures capable of breeding with any living thing. Yet neither Taniko nor Rat has ever mentioned Gaelion doing anything with the village monsters… Wait, maybe when Rat agreed with me in the monsters’ language, she was actually referring to this?

Given the vibe at the time, she probably just wanted to give me some chocolate or something like that. Even if it wasn’t meant as “friend chocolate” or anything like that, that conversation still makes sense. In fact, Taniko’s question was phrased as a question.
“Cure! Cureee, Cure!”
“Gaelion’s dream is to build a happy family with Master—I want lots and lots of kids—”
Is she… really telling the truth? When I point at Filo, the baby Gaelion nods repeatedly while struggling against the adult Gaelion’s grip. It seems Filo’s translation isn’t lying.
“Kids… you’re a male, aren’t you? And I’m a guy, too. What do you even think I am, anyway?”
“Cure! Cure, cure!”
‘Huh!? Stop it! Don’t say any more!’
Gaelion resisted with all his might, but the baby Gaelion let out a cry. And—Filo translated it.
“It’s okay—the Dragon Emperor can get a female pregnant even if the partner is a male—so please accept my confession—”
“…………… ……………………………What did you say?”
What did this guy just say? It can get a male pregnant?
“It’s fine if you have relationships with as many females as you want. But I want you, Master, to bear Gaelion’s child.”
Then, striking a dazzling pose, Gaelion cried out “Cure!” once more.
“I want to keep eating the grilled meat you make, Master, forever.”
Is this some kind of standard confession for dragons? You know, like, “Hey, the miso soup you made…” Just as I said that, Philo’s restraints came loose.
“Mmmph! What are you doing, Fitoria!”

As if throwing a tantrum, Filo glared at the stray strand of hair. As for the stray strand… it looked like it was thinking, “Gotcha!” Um, dragons can reproduce with any creature, and when it comes to the Dragon Emperor, even if the partner is a male… well, that doesn’t necessarily apply.
“I see, I see.”
I smiled and approached Gaelion.
“Kyuuaa…”
“Seriously… how foolish…”
Gaelion’s eyes sparkled, as if my sincerity had gotten through to him. But I grabbed Gaelion by the collar and threw him out of the house.
“Get out! Don’t ever come near me again!”
So this was the ulterior motive behind asking me for a hug as a Christmas present! Why do I have to get impregnated even though I’m a guy?! First Fohl, now Gaelion—do you guys want me to kill you?
“Kyuuaaah… Kyuuaaah…”
Gaelion scratched at the door with a scratching sound. I’ll have to give Taniko a stern talking-to later. Your dragon is trying to get me pregnant.
What a joke. And to think he even prepared this legendary chocolate just for that. What the hell is this! Seriously!
“Cure…”
Eventually, Gaelion seemed to give up and walked away.
“Filo wins!”
“I didn’t win.”
She’s the most normal one here in the sense that she’s a girl, but that doesn’t change the fact that she tried to attack me. There’s no winner here!
“Well then, Filo, I’m going to head back to Mel-chan’s place now.”
“Yeah, go ahead. Seriously… what a terrible day. Today, anyway.”

The only saving grace was that Sadeena was on her best behavior. Can she see into the future or something? Out of everyone except Raphtalia and Raph-chan, she scored the most points with her moves! That’s how I’d rate today. Filo left the house and traveled through the portal.
“Sigh…”
I’m more exhausted than usual today. Mainly because of Fohl and Gaelion. I guess I’ll go to bed early.

“”
So noisy… Stop howling like you just got dumped. With that, I got ready for bed and lay down. After a while… something strange started happening.
Drip… drip…
“Hmm…”

Something’s touching my cheek. Oh, so you guys are up to something, huh? Cut it out already. Do you guys have a grudge against me or something?! “Are you trying to attack me while I’m asleep, now that the girls aren’t here?!” I thought, opening my eyes.
“Wh—”
I was speechless. Something brown was stuck to the ceiling of my room, dripping onto me. “What the hell is this?!” I thought, checking what had landed on my cheek.
…It was chocolate.

The chocolate, clumped in lumps on the ceiling, began to wriggle. Then it spat something out with a “plop.” I think it was the box of chocolate Gaelion had been holding. Wait, Gaelion was supposed to have taken it home, right?

Come to think of it… the boss of the Chocolate Monsters was in the village, and I’d left him in the care of Taniko and Rat, but I hadn’t restrained him with a monster seal. In other words, we’d communicated, but he’s still wild! “Have you forgotten the favor I did you?” I thought, glaring at him, and his monster name appeared.
Legendary Super Chocolate Monster IV
…It’s powered up!? What does “IV” mean!? And… I catch a glimpse of something that looks like Gaelion’s tail. Was he swallowed up!? Do Chocolate Monsters have abilities like this!?

Come to think of it, I heard Gaelion let out an incredible howl earlier—was that his death cry? Oh no, I’m getting a terrible chill. Just to be safe, I’ll check more thoroughly. Doing this lets me see its level to some extent.
……Unmeasurable.
Why!? Could it be… that Gaelion’s chocolate caused it to rapidly level up and grow!? I feel like my shield is sounding an alarm.
“Shooting Star Shield EX!”

Using EX—a realm the other heroes can’t access—I generate a defensive barrier! The chocolate monster lands on top of the Shooting Star Shield EX. With a sizzling sound, the Shooting Star Shield starts to melt!?
Oh no! It seems to possess strength that’s no joke! Maybe I should’ve just killed it after all!? My instincts whisper to me to run away fast.
“Ugh…!”
The moment the Shooting Star Shield shattered, I leaped back and fled.
“Ah, big bro! You finally turned around—”
“Naofumi-sama! You were worried about me—”
As soon as I stepped out of the house, Fohl and Atla were arguing, but I ignored them and rushed past.
“Run!”
“Run…?”
“Run from what— Whoa!”
“Naofumi-sama—”

The Legendary Super Chocolate Monster IV burst through the front door with a splash and swallowed up Fohl and Atla. The very next moment, it became even more agile—as if it had powered up—and started chasing me. This is bad… Is this… a snowball effect? The more I run, the worse it seems to get. But… remembering that Gaelion exchange from earlier… if I get caught, I’ll probably end up getting impregnated!

After that, I escaped using my Portal Skills, and after a massive showdown, the incident was resolved—but I’d rather forget about it because I don’t want to remember. Specifically, it was the guys who really stepped up. Also, the women who don’t have a thing for me—basically, the female knights, Taniko, and Rishia.
Long live horse-manure chocolate! I never thought the day would come when I’d be grateful to this thing.
The Chocolate Monster’s goal was to deliver its love to me. To do that, it seems it could absorb anyone who had feelings for me to power up. I don’t get it.

As for the Chocolate Monster boss—the source of the problem—even though I tore it to pieces, it had resurrected by the next morning and was just hanging out in the village as usual. Right after that, I tore it to pieces again and this time used Magic to blast it away, but it had resurrected yet again by the next morning. I repeated this for about three days but couldn’t get rid of it, so with the help of Taniko and Rat, I forcibly bound it with a monster seal. That Valentine’s Day incident must have been a genuine case of it running amok—it wasn’t so much remorseful as it was just not putting up a fight.

Incidentally, after being freed from the chocolate, Fohl calmed down. Apparently, upon giving it some thought, he realized something was off, and he came to apologize later. Even though he was confused at the time, he seems to be reflecting on what he did, and he’s working harder than ever now.
As for Gaelion… he was just the same as always. However, since I felt so relieved, a murderous impulse sprouted in me—I even considered killing him. I’ll make sure to stay away from him from now on.
…It was the worst Valentine’s Day ever. Later, this incident came to be known as the “Rotten Valentine’s Day.”
I cut some scenes because they were too long.
